questions.question: Explain the difference between weather and climate, using Johannesburg as an example.
questions.expected_answer: Weather is the state of the air at a particular time, for example, a hot, stormy afternoon in Johannesburg today. Climate is the usual weather over about thirty years, described by temperature and rainfall: Johannesburg usually has warm summers with afternoon thunderstorms and cold, dry, sunny winters with frost.

questions.question: Describe the climates of the east coast, the Highveld and the Drakensberg.
questions.expected_answer: The east coast, like Durban, is warm and wet, with hot, humid, rainy summers and mild, dry winters. The Highveld has warm summers with thunderstorms and cold, dry winters with frost, because it is high. The Drakensberg has a cold mountain climate, with snow on the peaks in winter and cool, rainy summers.

questions.question: Describe the climates of the south-western Cape, the southern coast and the Karoo.
questions.expected_answer: The south-western Cape, like Cape Town, has a Mediterranean climate, with warm, dry summers and cool, wet winters. The southern coast, along the Garden Route, is mild with rain in all seasons. The Karoo is dry, with little, unreliable rain, hot summer days and cold winter nights.
